chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Idrees al-Harithi, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Mufazzal ibn Umar, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Mufazzal! Protect yourself from all people by [In the Name of Allah the Beneficent, the Merciful] and by [Say: He Allah is One]'
Recite them on your right, and on your left, and in front of you, and from behind you, and from above you, and from beneath you.
So whenever you go over to a tyrannous ruling authority, then recite them when you look at him, three times.
And close your left hand, nor releasing it until you come out from his presence.

key_terms.بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ: In the Name of Allah the Beneficent, the Merciful (Surah al-Fatiha opening)
key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Say: He Allah is One (Surah al-Ikhlas)

ai.seo_question: How to protect oneself from people and tyrants using Quranic recitation according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) instructs Mufazzal ibn Umar to recite Surah al-Fatiha and Surah al-Ikhlas as a means of protection from all people. The recitation is to be performed in all directions, and specifically when facing a tyrannical ruler, accompanied by a specific gesture of closing the left hand. This practice reflects the Shia tradition of using Quranic verses as spiritual armor (ta'wiz) against political oppression and the 'evil eye' of authority.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Idrees Al Harsy, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Mufazzal Bin Umra who said,
‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘O Mufazzal! Protect yourself from the people, all of them by [1:1] In the Name of Allah the Beneficent, the Merciful, and by [112:1] Say: He Allah is One (Chapter 112),
reciting it on your right, and on your left, and in front of you, and from behind you, and from above you, and from beneath you.
So whenever you go over to a tyrannous ruling authority, then recite it when you look at him, three times,
and close your left hand, nor releasing it until you come out from his presence’.
en.sarwar: 20. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Idris al-Harithi from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Mufaddal ibn ‘Umar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) said, ‘O Mufaddal, protect yourself from all people with this: ‘(I begin) in the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful’, and with Chapter 112 by reading toward each directions: right, left, front, back, above and below. When you enter in the presence of a tyranical ruler read it three times when looking at him, count it with your left hand and continue reading until you leave his presence.’”
